rows.notes: History, from Tri-State's SEC filings: the first HILT was board-approved and filed with FERC in August 2025 and rejected by FERC in October 2025 (Q3 2025 10-Q: "In August 2025, our Board approved and we filed with FERC a new tariff and pro forma agreement for high impact loads that have large load requirements, including data centers, into our system." and "In October 2025, FERC issued an order rejecting our tariff."); the 2026 filing drew a FERC deficiency letter in May 2026 and Tri-State's response in June 2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q). In August 2025 Tri-State also filed BYOR tariff amendments to expand the BYOR Program to high impact loads, accepted by FERC in October 2025 (2025 10-K, Bring Your Own Resource Program). Leads not used as values: Tri-State's own press release of 14 August 2026 on tristate.coop (read before its terms were read; terms bar robots, so not used) and a Colorado news report describe a 45 MW threshold (load additions over 45 MW at request or forecast to exceed 45 MW within four years), a security payment, a minimum term, minimum monthly demand and energy charges, and a 30-day compliance filing on agreements for Eastern Interconnection members; the 2025 filing's FERC docket is ER25-3316 per search results only (its copy on rtoinsider.com is refused by robots). Waits: the FERC order of August 2026 and the 2026 HILT filing (eLibrary accession numbers needed), and the compliance filing.

rows.rule_name: Schedule LL, Large Load Tariff (20 MW or more at over 80 percent load factor), with its companion Large Load Queue Service Request Process
rows.source_title: Large Load Tariff Schedule LL, Effective September 15, 2026 (Imperial Irrigation District)

quoted_clause.quote: Any customer with: (1) a monthly expected demand of 20 MW or more and (2) an expected load factor of greater than 80% must take service under this Schedule LL.

docket.searched: IID board action; no docket or resolution number is printed on Schedule LL or IID's Large Load Customers page

cites.quote: Effective September 15, 2026

On September 15, 2026, the IID Board of Directors approved Schedule LL, establishing a service process for new or expanded electrical loads that meet the tariff’s Large Load applicability requirements.

threshold_mw.value: monthly expected demand of 20 MW or more and expected load factor greater than 80 percent; facilities reaching the threshold by expansion are included; IID may aggregate facilities, meters or points of interconnection

cites.quote: Any customer with: (1) a monthly expected demand of 20 MW or more and (2) an expected load factor of greater than 80% must take service under this Schedule LL.
The applicability of this Schedule LL applies to facilities that trigger the identified threshold due to expansion.

min_demand.value: monthly energy charge on the higher of actual energy or 85 percent of contracted energy (Minimum Energy Charge); monthly demand charge on the higher of the highest 15-minute peak or 85 percent of Contract Demand (Minimum Demand Charge); a minimum renewable compliance cost charge on the Minimum Energy Charge energy

cites.quote: Eighty-five percent (85%) of Customer’s contracted for energy as established in the Electric Service Agreement (“Minimum Energy Charge”)
Eighty-five percent (85%) of the Contract Demand amount as established in the Electric Service Agreement (“Minimum Demand Charge”)
The costs associated with the District obtaining the necessary renewable energy associated with Customer’s Minimum Energy Charge energy (“Minimum Renewable Compliance Cost Charge”).

contract_term.value: initial term of not less than 15 years, set in the Electric Service Agreement; service continues after it unless terminated or modified; termination or modification requires at least 60 months written notice

cites.quote: The contract term will be identified in the Electric Service Agreement between the District and the Customer and will be for a period of not less than fifteen (15) years (the “Initial Contract Term”).

If a party wishes to terminate or modify either the Initial Contract Term or an Extension Term, that party must provide a minimum of sixty (60) months written notice to the other party of its intention to discontinue service under the terms of this Schedule LL.

collateral.value: Service Deposit of no less than three months of the highest estimated total monthly charges, in cash unless IID accepts other security; plus a Collateral Requirement of not less than IID's reasonably estimated exposure for up to 60 months, as a parental guaranty (A3 Moody's and A- S&P minimum ratings), standby letter of credit, surety bond or cash, maintained for the full service period; in the queue process, a Facilities Commitment Deposit of 50 percent of IID's preliminary estimate of applicant-funded facilities costs to advance to Phase II, and tiered study deposits of $100,000 (under 50 MW), $150,000 (50 to under 200 MW) or $200,000 (200 MW or more) plus $1,000 per MW of requested peak demand

cites.quote: The Service Deposit shall be no less than three (3) months of the Customer’s highest estimated total monthly charges, including energy, demand, and any applicable minimum charges.
The Initial Deposit shall be provided in cash, unless the District, in its sole discretion, agrees to accept an alternative form of security.
The amount of Collateral Requirement shall not be less than the District’s reasonably estimated exposure associated with serving the Customer for a period of up to sixty (60) months
A Parental Guaranty is only acceptable if Customer or its affiliate maintains an investment grade credit rating of: “A3” or higher by Moody’s, and (ii) “A-” or higher by S&P
The Collateral Requirement must be maintained for the full period of time that Customer takes service under Schedule LL.
A payment equal to fifty percent (50%) of IID’s preliminary estimate of the Applicant Funded Facilities Costs identified in the Phase I study report.

Less than 50 MW $100,000 plus $1,000 for each MW of Requested Peak Demand 50 MW or more, but less than 200 MW $150,000 plus $1,000 for each MW of Requested Peak Demand 200 MW or more $200,000 plus $1,000 for each MW of Requested Peak Demand

exit_fee.value: on termination or a contract capacity reduction during the Initial Contract Term: the remaining Minimum Charge for the terminated or reduced capacity for the rest of the Initial Contract Term, due on the effective date of the termination or reduction

cites.quote: The Exit Fee will be the remaining Minimum Charge for any terminated or reduced capacity for the remainder of the Initial Contract Term, as defined in the Electric Service Agreement.
The Exit Fee must be paid to the District upon the effective date of either the contract termination or capacity reduction.

study_timeline.value: completeness notice within 10 Business Days of the Stage 1 submission; Feasibility Assessment targeted within 30 Business Days; Phase I Study Authorization targeted within 20 Business Days of the Queue Position; Phase I System Impact Study report, best efforts within 90 Business Days of the Phase I authorization; Phase II report, best efforts within 90 Business Days of the Phase II authorization; 30 Business Days for the applicant to advance after the Phase I report

cites.quote: Within ten (10) Business Days after receiving the Stage 1 submission, IID will issue a written completeness notice or a deficiency notice identifying each missing requirement.
IID will target delivery of a written Feasibility Assessment within thirty (30) Business Days.
Within twenty (20) Business Days after IID assigns the request a Queue Position, or after formation of an applicable cluster, IID will target issuance of the Phase I Study Authorization.
The District will use best efforts to provide the Phase I Study report within ninety (90) Business Days after the Phase I Study Authorization is executed.
The District will use best efforts to provide the Phase II Study report within ninety (90) Business Days after the Phase II Study Authorization is executed.
Within thirty (30) Business Days after IID delivers the Phase I Study Report and the Phase II advancement package, an Applicant seeking to proceed must provide:

rows.notes: The Queue Service Request Process also sets a fixed $20,000 non-refundable application fee, a 10 Business Day cure period, first-ready, first-served administration, and serial or cluster studies. Service under Schedule LL is full requirements service at 69 kV or higher and interruptible at IID's sole discretion (p. 3). The customer pays the actual costs of all studies and bears the cost of substations and upgrades (pp. 2 to 3).
